# pool

```go
import "github.com/kitsunium/sdk/pkg/v1/concur/pool"
```

Package pool runs tasks on a fixed set of long-lived workers fed by a bounded queue: a refusal when there is no room, a drain, and a task's panic kept on its worker instead of taking the process down.

```
p := pool.NewPool(ctx, pool.Config{Workers: 8, Queue: 64,
    OnPanic: func(pv pool.PanicValue) { log.Print(pv) },
})
if err := p.Submit(ctx, handle); errors.Is(err, pool.PoolFull) {
    // shed the load: every worker busy and the queue full
}
err := p.Drain(ctx) // runs what is queued, then the workers exit
```

It is the SDK's own worker pool, published as an alias of the kernel package its services run on (ADR 0159 §4, ADR 0216).

### When to use it

When the same kind of work arrives for as long as a service lives — a request pipeline, a probe per check, a send per batch — and its concurrency must be bounded without a goroutine per task. For one fan-out that is waited on once, the group package is the tool; for one daemon goroutine, worker.

### Room, and the refusal

Without a queue ([Config](#Config).Queue 0) [Pool](#Pool).Submit hands the task to an idle worker or returns [PoolFull](#PoolFull) at once: it never parks. With a queue, a full one is waited on within the submitter's context, and PoolFull then wraps that context's error. After [Pool](#Pool).Drain or [Pool](#Pool).Stop, Submit returns [PoolClosed](#PoolClosed).

### Context

A task receives the pool's context — the one given to [NewPool](#NewPool), cancelled by Stop —, not the submitter's: the values a task needs travel in its closure, which is what keeps a Submit free of allocation.

### Faults

A task's panic is recovered on its worker into a [PanicValue](#PanicValue) — the value and the worker's stack — handed to [Config](#Config).OnPanic, and the worker serves the next task. Without an OnPanic the panic is raised again: a fault nobody observes is never swallowed. A task's error goes to [Config](#Config).OnError.

<a name="Config"></a>
## type [Config](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/concur/pool/gen_facade.go>)

Config sizes a [Pool](#Pool): Workers, how many tasks run at once (at least one); Queue, how many may wait (zero refuses at once when every worker is busy); OnPanic, which receives a task's recovered panic (nil raises it again); and OnError, which receives a task's error (nil discards it). The zero Config is usable.

```go
type Config = kpool.Config
```

Config is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/kernel/concur/pool.Config`, declared as:

```go
type Config struct {
	// Workers is how many tasks run at once, each on a long-lived worker; a
	// value below 1 is 1.
	Workers int
	// Queue is how many submitted tasks may wait for a worker. Zero is no
	// queue: Submit refuses at once when every worker is busy. A positive
	// queue makes a Submit that finds it full wait, within its context. A
	// negative value is zero.
	Queue   int
	// OnPanic receives a task's panic, recovered on its worker, which then
	// serves the next task. Nil raises the panic again on the worker: a fault
	// nobody observes is not swallowed, and the process ends as it would for
	// a bare goroutine.
	OnPanic func(p PanicValue)
	// OnError receives a task's non-nil error, which has no caller to return
	// to. Nil discards it.
	OnError func(err error)
}
```

## type [PanicValue](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/concur/pool/gen_facade.go>)

PanicValue carries a task's panic to [Config](#Config).OnPanic: Raised, the value the panic carried, and Stack, the stack of the worker that ran the task. It is not an error: a panic is a programming fault.

<a name="Pool"></a>
## type [Pool](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/pkg/v1/concur/pool/gen_facade.go>)

Pool is a fixed set of workers consuming a bounded queue of tasks.

[Pool](#Pool).Submit hands a task over, or returns [PoolFull](#PoolFull) when there is no room and [PoolClosed](#PoolClosed) after Drain or Stop; [Pool](#Pool).Drain stops accepting, runs what is queued and waits for the workers within its context; [Pool](#Pool).Stop abandons the queue, cancels the running tasks' context and waits for them within its context. Safe for concurrent use; the zero value is NOT usable, build it with [NewPool](#NewPool).

```go
type Pool = kpool.Pool
```

Pool is an alias of `github.com/kitsunium/sdk/internal/kernel/concur/pool.Pool`, declared as:

```go
type Pool struct{}
```

<a name="Pool.Drain"></a>
### func \(Pool\) [Drain](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/kernel/concur/pool/pool.go>)

```go
func (*Pool) Drain(ctx context.Context) error
```

Drain stops accepting tasks, lets the workers run every task already queued, and waits for them to exit within ctx: nil once they have, ctx's error when it ends first — the workers then go on until the queue is empty; Stop abandons it. Idempotent.

<a name="Pool.Stop"></a>
### func \(Pool\) [Stop](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/kernel/concur/pool/pool.go>)

```go
func (*Pool) Stop(ctx context.Context) error
```

Stop stops accepting tasks, abandons those still queued — they never run —, cancels the context the running ones received, and waits for them within ctx: nil once every worker has exited, ctx's error when it ends first. A task that ignores its context cannot be stopped from outside. Idempotent.

<a name="Pool.Submit"></a>
### func \(Pool\) [Submit](<https://github.com/kitsunium/sdk/blob/main/internal/kernel/concur/pool/pool.go>)

```go
func (*Pool) Submit(ctx context.Context, task Task) error
```

Submit hands task to the pool. Without a queue it is taken by an idle worker or refused with PoolFull at once — never parked. With one, a full queue is waited on until ctx ends, which returns PoolFull wrapping ctx's error. After Drain or Stop it returns PoolClosed. A task accepted runs exactly once, unless Stop abandons it first. A nil task panics.
